# statsd_count in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/macro.statsd_count.html

```
macro_rules! statsd_count {
    ($key:expr, $val:expr) => { ... };
    ($key:expr, $val:expr, $($tag_key:expr => $tag_val:expr),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emit a counter using the default global client, optionally with tags

The counter will use the prefix from the default global client combined with the provided key.

Any errors encountered sending metrics will be handled by the error handler registered with the default global client. This error handler is a no-op unless explicitly set. Callers should set the error handler for the default client if you wish to handle these errors (by logging them or something similar).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This macro will panic if the default global client has not been set when
it is invoked (via `cadence_macros::set_global_default`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
use cadence_macros::statsd_count;
let client = StatsdClient::builder("my.prefix", NopMetricSink)
    .with_error_handler(|e| { eprintln!("metric error: {}", e) })
    .build();
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123);
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c|#tag:val"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val");
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c|#tag:val,another:thing"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Only key-value style tags are supported. Value style tags are not
supported, e.g. `builder.with_tag_value("val")`.

---

# statsd_distribution in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/macro.statsd_distribution.html

```
macro_rules! statsd_distribution {
    ($key:expr, $val:expr) => { ... };
    ($key:expr, $val:expr, $($tag_key:expr => $tag_val:expr),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emit a distribution using the default global client, optionally with tags

The distribution will use the prefix from the default global client combined with the provided key.

Any errors encountered sending metrics will be handled by the error handler registered with the default global client. This error handler is a no-op unless explicitly set. Callers should set the error handler for the default client if you wish to handle these errors (by logging them or something similar).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This macro will panic if the default global client has not been set when
it is invoked (via `cadence_macros::set_global_default`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
use cadence_macros::statsd_distribution;
let client = StatsdClient::builder("my.prefix", NopMetricSink)
    .with_error_handler(|e| { eprintln!("metric error: {}", e) })
    .build();
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
// "my.prefix.some.distribution:123|d"
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123);
// "my.prefix.some.distribution:123|d|#tag:val"
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val");
// "my.prefix.some.distribution:123|d|#tag:val,another:thing"
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Only key-value style tags are supported. Value style tags are not
supported, e.g. `builder.with_tag_value("val")`.

---

# statsd_gauge in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/macro.statsd_gauge.html

```
macro_rules! statsd_gauge {
    ($key:expr, $val:expr) => { ... };
    ($key:expr, $val:expr, $($tag_key:expr => $tag_val:expr),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emit a gauge using the default global client, optionally with tags

The gauge will use the prefix from the default global client combined with the provided key.

Any errors encountered sending metrics will be handled by the error handler registered with the default global client. This error handler is a no-op unless explicitly set. Callers should set the error handler for the default client if you wish to handle these errors (by logging them or something similar).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This macro will panic if the default global client has not been set when
it is invoked (via `cadence_macros::set_global_default`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
use cadence_macros::statsd_gauge;
let client = StatsdClient::builder("my.prefix", NopMetricSink)
    .with_error_handler(|e| { eprintln!("metric error: {}", e) })
    .build();
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
// "my.prefix.some.gauge:123|g"
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123);
// "my.prefix.some.gauge:123|g|#tag:val"
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val");
// "my.prefix.some.gauge:123|g|#tag:val,another:thing"
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Only key-value style tags are supported. Value style tags are not
supported, e.g. `builder.with_tag_value("val")`.

---

# get_global_default in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/fn.get_global_default.html

`pub fn get_global_default() -> `[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[StatsdClient](https://docs.rs/cadence/1.8.0/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence/client/struct.StatsdClient.html)>, [GlobalDefaultNotSet](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalDefaultNotSet.html)>## Expand description

Get a reference to the global default `StatsdClient` instance

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This method will return an error if the global default has not been
previously set via the `set_global_default` method.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
let global_client = cadence_macros::get_global_default();
assert!(global_client.is_err());
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", NopMetricSink);
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
let global_client = cadence_macros::get_global_default();
assert!(global_client.is_ok());
```

---

# is_global_default_set in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/fn.is_global_default_set.html

`pub fn is_global_default_set() -> `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)## Expand description

Return true if the global default `StatsdClient` is set, false otherwise

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
assert!(!cadence_macros::is_global_default_set());
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", NopMetricSink);
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
assert!(cadence_macros::is_global_default_set());
```

# set_global_default in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence_macros/fn.set_global_default.html

`pub fn set_global_default(client: `[StatsdClient](https://docs.rs/cadence/1.8.0/aarch64-apple-darwin/cadence/client/struct.StatsdClient.html))## Expand description

Set the global default `StatsdClient` instance

If the global default client has already been set, this method does nothing.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", NopMetricSink);
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
```

---

# cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cadence-macros/1.8.0/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence_macros/

## Expand description

An extensible Statsd client for Rust!

Cadence is a fast and flexible way to emit Statsd metrics from your application.
The `cadence-macros` crate provides some wrappers to eliminate much of the boilerplate
that is often needed to emit metrics along with any tags that are associated with
them.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- [Support](https://docs.rs/cadence/)for emitting counters, timers, histograms, distributions, gauges, meters, and sets to Statsd over UDP (or optionally Unix sockets).
- Support for alternate backends via the `MetricSink`trait.
- Support for [Datadog](https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/dogstatsd/)style metrics tags.
- [Macros](https://docs.rs/cadence-macros/)to simplify common calls to emit metrics
- A simple yet flexible API for sending metrics.

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

To make use of `cadence-macros` in your project, add it as a dependency in your `Cargo.toml` file.

```
[dependencies]
cadence-macros = "x.y.z"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

To make use of the macros in this crate, you’ll need to set a global default Statsd client.
Configure a `cadence::StatsdClient` as usual and use the `set_global_default` function to
set it as the default. After that, you can make use of the macros in this crate.

```
use std::net::UdpSocket;
use std::time::Duration;
use cadence::prelude::*;
use cadence::{StatsdClient, QueuingMetricSink, BufferedUdpMetricSink, DEFAULT_PORT};
use cadence_macros::{statsd_count, statsd_time, statsd_gauge, statsd_meter, statsd_histogram, statsd_distribution, statsd_set};
// Normal setup for a high-performance Cadence instance
let socket = UdpSocket::bind("0.0.0.0:0").unwrap();
socket.set_nonblocking(true).unwrap();
let host = ("metrics.example.com", DEFAULT_PORT);
let udp_sink = BufferedUdpMetricSink::from(host, socket).unwrap();
let queuing_sink = QueuingMetricSink::from(udp_sink);
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", queuing_sink);
// Set the default client to use for macro calls
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
// Macros!
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123);
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_time!("some.timer", 123);
statsd_time!("some.timer", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_time!("some.timer", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_time!("some.timer", Duration::from_millis(123), "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123);
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123);
statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123);
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", Duration::from_nanos(123), "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123);
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_set!("some.set", 123);
statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Some limitations with the current implemenation of Cadence macros are described below

- Value tags are not supported. For example the following style of tag cannot be
set when using macros: `client.count_with_tags("some.counter", 123).with_tag_value("beta").send()`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_count.html)- count
- Emit a counter using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_distribution.html)- distribution
- Emit a distribution using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_gauge.html)- gauge
- Emit a gauge using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_histogram.html)- histogram
- Emit a histogram using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_meter.html)- meter
- Emit a meter using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_set.html)- set
- Emit a set using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_time.html)- time
- Emit a timer using the default global client, optionally with tags

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalDefaultNotSet.html)- Default - NotSet
- Error indicating that a global default `StatsdClient`was not set when a call to`get_global_default`was made.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_global_default.html)- global_ - default
- Get a reference to the global default `StatsdClient`instance
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_global_default_set.html)- global_ - default_ - set
- Return true if the global default `StatsdClient`is set, false otherwise
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_global_default.html)- global_ - default
- Set the global default `StatsdClient`instance

---

statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", Duration::from_nanos(123), "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123);
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
statsd_set!("some.set", 123);
statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val");
statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Some limitations with the current implemenation of Cadence macros are described below

- Value tags are not supported. For example the following style of tag cannot be
set when using macros: `client.count_with_tags("some.counter", 123).with_tag_value("beta").send()`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_count.html)- count
- Emit a counter using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_distribution.html)- distribution
- Emit a distribution using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_gauge.html)- gauge
- Emit a gauge using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_histogram.html)- histogram
- Emit a histogram using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_meter.html)- meter
- Emit a meter using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_set.html)- set
- Emit a set using the default global client, optionally with tags
- [statsd_](https://docs.rs/macro.statsd_time.html)- time
- Emit a timer using the default global client, optionally with tags

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Global](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalDefaultNotSet.html)- Default - NotSet
- Error indicating that a global default `StatsdClient`was not set when a call to`get_global_default`was made.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_global_default.html)- global_ - default
- Get a reference to the global default `StatsdClient`instance
- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_global_default_set.html)- global_ - default_ - set
- Return true if the global default `StatsdClient`is set, false otherwise
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_global_default.html)- global_ - default
- Set the global default `StatsdClient`instance

# lib.rs - source

# cadence_macros/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// Cadence - An extensible Statsd client for Rust!
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//
[3](https://docs.rs#3)// Copyright 2020-2021 Nick Pillitteri
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//
[5](https://docs.rs#5)// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 <LICENSE-APACHE or
[6](https://docs.rs#6)// http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0> or the MIT license
[7](https://docs.rs#7)// <LICENSE-MIT or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT>, at your
[8](https://docs.rs#8)// option. This file may not be copied, modified, or distributed
[9](https://docs.rs#9)// except according to those terms.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! An extensible Statsd client for Rust!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! Cadence is a fast and flexible way to emit Statsd metrics from your application.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! The `cadence-macros` crate provides some wrappers to eliminate much of the boilerplate
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! that is often needed to emit metrics along with any tags that are associated with
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! them.
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! ## Features
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! * [Support](https://docs.rs/cadence/) for emitting counters, timers, histograms, distributions,
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!   gauges, meters, and sets to Statsd over UDP (or optionally Unix sockets).
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! * Support for alternate backends via the `MetricSink` trait.
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! * Support for [Datadog](https://docs.datadoghq.com/developers/dogstatsd/) style metrics tags.
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! * [Macros](https://docs.rs/cadence-macros/) to simplify common calls to emit metrics
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! * A simple yet flexible API for sending metrics.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ## Install
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! To make use of `cadence-macros` in your project, add it as a dependency in your `Cargo.toml` file.
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! ```toml
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! [dependencies]
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! cadence-macros = "x.y.z"
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! ```
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! ## Usage
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! To make use of the macros in this crate, you'll need to set a global default Statsd client.
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! Configure a `cadence::StatsdClient` as usual and use the `set_global_default` function to
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! set it as the default. After that, you can make use of the macros in this crate.
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! ```rust,no_run
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! use std::net::UdpSocket;
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! use std::time::Duration;
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! use cadence::prelude::*;
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//! use cadence::{StatsdClient, QueuingMetricSink, BufferedUdpMetricSink, DEFAULT_PORT};
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! use cadence_macros::{statsd_count, statsd_time, statsd_gauge, statsd_meter, statsd_histogram, statsd_distribution, statsd_set};
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! // Normal setup for a high-performance Cadence instance
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! let socket = UdpSocket::bind("0.0.0.0:0").unwrap();
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! socket.set_nonblocking(true).unwrap();
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//!
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! let host = ("metrics.example.com", DEFAULT_PORT);
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! let udp_sink = BufferedUdpMetricSink::from(host, socket).unwrap();
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! let queuing_sink = QueuingMetricSink::from(udp_sink);
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", queuing_sink);
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! // Set the default client to use for macro calls
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! // Macros!
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//! statsd_count!("some.counter", 123);
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val");
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//! statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//!
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//! statsd_time!("some.timer", 123);
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! statsd_time!("some.timer", 123, "tag" => "val");
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//! statsd_time!("some.timer", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! statsd_time!("some.timer", Duration::from_millis(123), "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//!
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//! statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123);
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val");
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//! statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//! statsd_gauge!("some.gauge", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123);
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123, "tag" => "val");
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! statsd_meter!("some.meter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//!
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123);
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val");
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//! statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", Duration::from_nanos(123), "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//! statsd_histogram!("some.histogram", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//!
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123);
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val");
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! statsd_distribution!("some.distribution", 123.123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//!
[91](https://docs.rs#91)//! statsd_set!("some.set", 123);
[92](https://docs.rs#92)//! statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val");
[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! statsd_set!("some.set", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
[94](https://docs.rs#94)//! ```
[95](https://docs.rs#95)//!
[96](https://docs.rs#96)//! ## Limitations
[97](https://docs.rs#97)//!
[98](https://docs.rs#98)//! Some limitations with the current implemenation of Cadence macros are described below
[99](https://docs.rs#99)//!
[100](https://docs.rs#100)//! * Value tags are not supported. For example the following style of tag cannot be
[101](https://docs.rs#101)//!   set when using macros: `client.count_with_tags("some.counter", 123).with_tag_value("beta").send()`
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)pub use crate::state::{
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    get_global_default, is_global_default_set, set_global_default, GlobalDefaultNotSet, SingletonHolder,
[106](https://docs.rs#106)};
[107](https://docs.rs#107)

[109](https://docs.rs#109)mod state;

# statsd_count in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence_macros/macro.statsd_count.html

```
macro_rules! statsd_count {
    ($key:expr, $val:expr) => { ... };
    ($key:expr, $val:expr, $($tag_key:expr => $tag_val:expr),*) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Emit a counter using the default global client, optionally with tags

The counter will use the prefix from the default global client combined with the provided key.

Any errors encountered sending metrics will be handled by the error handler registered with the default global client. This error handler is a no-op unless explicitly set. Callers should set the error handler for the default client if you wish to handle these errors (by logging them or something similar).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This macro will panic if the default global client has not been set when
it is invoked (via `cadence_macros::set_global_default`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
use cadence_macros::statsd_count;
let client = StatsdClient::builder("my.prefix", NopMetricSink)
    .with_error_handler(|e| { eprintln!("metric error: {}", e) })
    .build();
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123);
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c|#tag:val"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val");
// "my.prefix.some.counter:123|c|#tag:val,another:thing"
statsd_count!("some.counter", 123, "tag" => "val", "another" => "thing");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

Only key-value style tags are supported. Value style tags are not
supported, e.g. `builder.with_tag_value("val")`.

---

# GlobalDefaultNotSet in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence_macros/struct.GlobalDefaultNotSet.html

`pub struct GlobalDefaultNotSet;`## Expand description

Error indicating that a global default `StatsdClient` was not set
when a call to `get_global_default` was made.

# get_global_default in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence_macros/fn.get_global_default.html

`pub fn get_global_default() -> `[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[StatsdClient](https://docs.rs/cadence/1.8.0/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence/client/struct.StatsdClient.html)>, [GlobalDefaultNotSet](https://docs.rs/struct.GlobalDefaultNotSet.html)>## Expand description

Get a reference to the global default `StatsdClient` instance

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This method will return an error if the global default has not been
previously set via the `set_global_default` method.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
let global_client = cadence_macros::get_global_default();
assert!(global_client.is_err());
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", NopMetricSink);
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
let global_client = cadence_macros::get_global_default();
assert!(global_client.is_ok());
```

---

# is_global_default_set in cadence_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cadence-macros/latest/target-redirect/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/cadence_macros/fn.is_global_default_set.html

`pub fn is_global_default_set() -> `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)## Expand description

Return true if the global default `StatsdClient` is set, false otherwise

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cadence::{StatsdClient, NopMetricSink};
assert!(!cadence_macros::is_global_default_set());
let client = StatsdClient::from_sink("my.prefix", NopMetricSink);
cadence_macros::set_global_default(client);
assert!(cadence_macros::is_global_default_set());
```
